correctness.rationale: For every two-subset the Nyström Schur residual is the inverse grounded precision, whose trace equals the logarithmic derivative of its positive determinant polynomial. All classes through m=7 are compared by checked exact integer coefficient identities; the seven-rim decisive difference is twice a polynomial with one negative constant and strictly positive other coefficients, hence exactly one crossing. Unscreened hub dominance for m>=7 follows from the explicit bounded Green-function formula and an independently exact m=7,8 table; high-screening hub avoidance follows from a strict (m-3)/mu^2 leading coefficient. The packaged standalone verifier passed 2760 exact integer/rational assertions. Finite experiments are not relied on for unbounded m.

value.rationale: The seven-rim wheel is the minimal natural member of a network family exhibiting a design reversal under screened Gaussian precision; this is established by complete m=3..7 orbit classifications, not an arbitrary small graph choice. Exact critical design/tie sets and a confirmed high-screening effect for all larger wheels make this a structural A-optimal sensor/leader benchmark. The result is restricted to precisely these covariance and graph assumptions and is not claimed to improve general algorithms.
